students.text: Students can protect the environment by reducing plastic, planting trees, and spreading awareness in schools and communities.
Clean water and soil are essential. Students should organize local cleanup drives and avoid littering in nearby rivers and parks.
Switch off unused electronics, use renewable energy where possible, and educate family and friends on eco-friendly habits.
Participate in tree planting events. Every tree helps reduce carbon dioxide, provides oxygen, and supports wildlife.

farmers.text: Farmers protect the environment using organic fertilizers, crop rotation, and natural pest control.
Sustainable water management is key. Using rainwater harvesting, drip irrigation and avoiding chemical runoff preserves rivers.
Farmers can also plant trees along fields, maintain biodiversity, and practice zero-tillage methods to improve soil health.
Composting kitchen and farm waste reduces landfills and provides natural fertilizer, closing the loop in sustainable farming.

others.text: Volunteers, teachers, and environmentalists guide communities in reducing pollution and planting trees.
Community workshops, awareness campaigns, and clean-up drives make environmental protection a collective effort.
Everyone can contribute by using eco-friendly products, reducing energy use, and supporting sustainable businesses.
Encourage local governments to maintain parks, plant trees, and promote green initiatives for future generations.
